headline: Revenue climbs on travel demand, fuel spike sinks profit
summary_short: American Airlines posted Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16,735M, up 16.3% y/y on strong passenger demand, but an 83.3% jump in fuel expense (on a 77.1% higher average fuel price) drove operating income down 60.7% to $446M and net income down 88.1% to $71M ($0.11 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Revenue rose 16.3% y/y to $16.7B as PRASM grew 10.0% on strong travel demand and yield rose 11.9%; cargo (+29.7%) and loyalty-linked other revenue (+17.9%) also grew. Costs rose faster (+22.9%) as fuel expense jumped 83.3% on a 77.1% higher average fuel price and added capacity; CASM rose 16.5% to 19.90 cents, while CASM ex-fuel/special-items/profit-sharing rose a milder 2.9% to 13.93 cents on higher maintenance costs. Operating income fell 60.7% y/y to $446M; net income fell 88.1% to $71M ($0.11 diluted EPS). Cash rose to $1.1B; net debt eased 4.2% y/y to $27.1B after refinancing several credit facilities.

drivers.explanation: The 10-Q attributes the period-over-period profit decline to higher operating expenses, chiefly aircraft fuel, salaries and other operating costs, partly offset by higher passenger revenue.
Growth was driven by higher passenger revenue on strong domestic and international demand (PRASM +10.0%, yield +11.9%), plus cargo and loyalty-linked other-revenue gains.
Not a company-disclosed line; margin compression follows arithmetically from operating costs (+22.9%) outpacing revenue growth (+16.3%), led by the fuel-cost spike.
CASM rose 16.5% to 19.90 cents, which the filing says was primarily driven by higher fuel, maintenance and other operating expense per available seat mile.
Tracks the operating-income decline described above; depreciation and amortization were little changed y/y per the shard.
The 10-Q states the decline was principally driven by higher aircraft fuel, salaries/wages and other operating expenses, offset in part by higher passenger revenue.
Mirrors the pretax income decline; the quarter's income tax provision was $36M, versus a much larger pretax base a year earlier.
Tracks the net income decline; diluted weighted-average share count was little changed y/y (662.6M vs 660.4M).
Rose after 2026 refinancings, including new/incremental term loans and EETC/equipment-note proceeds, partly offset by repayments of higher-rate notes and a fuel-financing payoff.
Eased despite higher gross long-term debt, as total cash and restricted cash also rose; the filing does not decompose net debt directly.
